question.text: 'Aravalli Impact Ventures AIF-II' is a Category I AIF (Social Impact Fund) targeting INR 500 crore. Ms. Neha Kulkarni, the manager, is setting the sponsor's continuing interest / GP commitment. Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, what is the MINIMUM sponsor/manager commitment requirement for a Category I/II AIF, and why do most managers voluntarily commit MORE?

answer.text: Minimum is 2.5% or INR 5 crore (lower of the two) for Category I/II — managers voluntarily exceed this to signal 'skin in the game' to anchor LPs and as a GP commitment negotiation point
Minimum is 10% or INR 25 crore (lower of the two) — managers don't voluntarily exceed this
Minimum is 5% or INR 10 crore (higher of the two) — no voluntary excess
No minimum; entirely commercial negotiation with LPs

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI (AIF) Regulations (referenced in the chapter's Section I disclosures), minimum sponsor/manager commitment for Category I/II is lower of 2.5% of corpus or INR 5 crore. Managers typically commit MORE (often 5–10%) as a 'skin in the game' signal to sophisticated LPs, especially anchor LPs who explicitly negotiate higher GP commitment in side letters. The Trap: 10%/INR 25 cr is not the SEBI minimum. 5%/INR 10 cr is not correct. No-minimum is false — SEBI prescribes a floor. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A tests this at recall level. XIX-C requires connecting the regulatory floor to the commercial negotiation — anchor LPs may demand 5%+ GP commitment regardless of the floor. Manager's Pro-Tip: If anchor LPs demand >5% GP commitment, consider a GP co-investment SPV with warehoused participation — preserves your economics while satisfying LP 'alignment of interests' concerns.
